Flagged under this shape as a deliberately-provided kill switch for an authentication control rather than an accidental defect; a verifier should confirm whether it is set in deployed/compose configuration.

lead.text: All four regex literals in the `publicRoutes` authentication allowlist (packages/backend/src/api/v1/auth/utils.ts lines 63, 71, 72, 76) are missing `^` and `$` anchors, and are consumed with `route.test(ctx.path)` (line 85), which has SUBSTRING semantics — unlike the plain-string entries in the same array, which are compared with strict equality (`route === ctx.path`). The literals are `new RegExp(`/auth/.+`)`, `new RegExp(`/v1/runs/.+/public`)`, `new RegExp(`/v1/runs/.+/feedback`)` and `new RegExp(`/v1/datasets/.+`)`. Consequently ANY request path that merely CONTAINS one of these fragments is classified as public and skips verifyJwt — e.g. a path like `/v1/users/auth/x` or `/v1/orgs/v1/datasets/x` satisfies `isPublicRoute`. `.+` also matches `/`, so the patterns span arbitrarily many path segments rather than one. This makes the allowlist's blast radius depend on route-table coincidences instead of an explicit list, and any future route whose path embeds `/auth/` or `/v1/datasets/` silently becomes unauthenticated. Anchoring each literal (`^/v1/datasets/[^/]+$`) and splitting by HTTP method is the fix.
